info.title: kube-noob REST API
info.description: The kube-noob tools as JSON over HTTP, beside MCP. Bearer token as for MCP.

id.description: A report id as POST /v1/alert-reports returned it, e.g. 20261111T101500.123456Z-<24 hex digits>.
id.title: Id

payload.description: An Alertmanager webhook body (version 4), the Alertmanager API's alert list or Prometheus's /api/v1/alerts, as JSON. Each alert is reported on its own; an openshift_version or version label holding an OpenShift release narrows the reported issues to it.
payload.title: Payload

limit.description: How many of the newest reports to list.
limit.title: Limit

manifests.description: One or more YAML documents (Kubernetes/OpenShift objects).
manifests.title: Manifests

exceptions.description: An exception list (YAML, apiVersion kube-noob.io/v1, kind ExceptionList): each entry names a rule, a scope, an owner, a reason and an expiry date. Active entries hide the findings they cover; expired and refused entries are reported and fail the gate.
exceptions.title: Exceptions

partial_bundle.description: Set when these documents are only part of a namespace (one file, a diff, staged changes). Rules that fire because another object is absent -- no NetworkPolicy selects this workload, no PodDisruptionBudget, a StorageClass not declared here -- are then not evaluated, because from a partial bundle they cannot tell a real gap from an object you did not pass. The report says so in its assumptions.
partial_bundle.title: Partial Bundle

cni.description: The cluster's CNI as NAME or NAME:VERSION (calico:3.32, ovn-kubernetes, cilium:1.18). No manifest states it, so KN-N014 -- an AdminNetworkPolicy or BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy the CNI stopped enforcing, which Calico did in 3.32 without reporting an error -- is NOT EVALUATED unless you name it, rather than counted clean.
cni.title: Cni

compact.description: Return the same report with each rule's constant fields (title, severity, stage, category, remediation, citations, stackroxPolicies, controls) collected once into a `ruleInfo` map keyed by rule id instead of repeated on every finding. Lossless and about a third smaller on a report where rules fire more than once; the findings keep their order, rule id, resource, line and message. Off by default so the flat shape stays what it was.
compact.title: Compact

text.description: Events, `describe` output, logs, CLI errors, status JSON, Ceph health output (`ceph health detail`, `ceph status`, their JSON or a CephCluster) or an Alertmanager webhook payload (its alerts are read as text; an `openshift_version` or `version` label gives the version).
text.title: Text

version.description: The cluster's OpenShift version (4.20 or 4.20.8): leaves out reported issues already fixed there.
version.title: Version

text.description: Anything pasted: events, describe output, logs, an Alertmanager payload, Ceph health output (ceph health detail or ceph status, text or JSON), a policy denial, a ticket, manifests or a Helm template, a build log, a Containerfile, an SBOM or scanner report, or a question.
text.title: Text

text.description: An error message, events, logs or a symptom in words. Past 100,000 characters only the end is matched, and the result says so (inputTruncated).
text.title: Text

version.description: The cluster's OpenShift version (4.20 or 4.20.8): keeps only issues that can affect it.
version.title: Version

text.description: An error, events, logs, a symptom in words or an Alertmanager webhook payload.
text.title: Text

version.description: The cluster's OpenShift version: entries already fixed there are shown as retired.
version.title: Version

operators.description: Installed operators and their versions, name -> version.
operators.title: Operators

include_proposed.description: Also show entries not yet approved by a reviewer.
include_proposed.title: Include Proposed

path.description: Absolute path of a must-gather directory or .tar, .tar.gz or .tgz archive on the machine the server runs on (under mustGather.allowedDir when it is set). Nothing is extracted or run; Secrets are never read.
path.title: Path

top.description: How many findings to return, most severe first.
top.title: Top

case_draft.description: Also return caseDraft: a support case draft with placeholders for what only you know.
case_draft.title: Case Draft

source.description: Where the connection starts: namespace/name of a workload (namespace/kind/name when names clash), namespace:key=value,... for a set of pod labels, or an IP address / CIDR outside the cluster.
source.title: Source

destination.description: Where it goes: namespace/name of a workload (namespace/kind/name when names clash), namespace:key=value,... for a set of pod labels, or an IP address / CIDR outside the cluster.
destination.title: Destination

port.description: Destination port number (1-65535) or a named container port.
port.title: Port

cni.description: The cluster's CNI as NAME or NAME:VERSION (calico:3.32, ovn-kubernetes, cilium:1.18). Given, it decides whether AdminNetworkPolicy and BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy are enforced at all: Calico ignores both from 3.32 onward, so policies in that tier are reported as inert instead of deciding the answer, and a CNI whose enforcement is undocumented makes the verdict undetermined rather than guessing either way.
cni.title: Cni

manifests.description: The NetworkPolicies and the workloads they apply to (Deployments, Pods ...); add Namespace objects when policies select namespaces by label.
manifests.title: Manifests

policies.description: One or more legacy Kyverno policies (YAML): kyverno.io ClusterPolicy, Policy, ClusterCleanupPolicy, CleanupPolicy or PolicyException. Other documents are listed and skipped; Secrets are not read.
policies.title: Policies

drafts.description: Include a draft CEL policy for each rule whose fields all map directly, and a kyverno test fixture skeleton per policy (good and bad resources run against the legacy rule and the draft).
drafts.title: Drafts

text.description: An Alertmanager payload, events, a ClusterOperator, pod status, logs or an error in words.
text.title: Text

current.description: The OpenShift version the cluster runs, x.y.z, e.g. 4.20.3.
current.title: Current

target.description: The version to update to, x.y.z, e.g. 4.21.4.
target.title: Target

arch.description: The release architecture (multi for a multi-architecture payload). Without it, every architecture is checked and a risk declared for some of them only says which.
arch.title: Arch

AlertmanagerPayload.description: An Alertmanager webhook body (version 4: receiver, status, commonLabels, alerts[] with status, labels and annotations), the Alertmanager API v2 alert list, or Prometheus's /api/v1/alerts, as JSON. Read bounded: 500 alerts, 64 labels, 2,000 characters a value, control characters dropped; the server's body limit is 1.5 MiB. Sources: https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/#webhook_config and https://github.com/prometheus/alertmanager/blob/main/api/v2/openapi.yaml

post.summary: Paste anything: recognised, routed to every analyser, one answer
post.description: Start here for anything the user pastes. Names what the input is (events, pod status, logs, an Alertmanager payload, a policy denial, a ticket, manifests, a Helm template, a build log, a Containerfile, an SBOM or scanner report, a packet trace, must-gather paths, a question; several at once) and runs every analyser that applies: diagnosis with reported issues and team memory, the denial explainer, the audit, the documentation. Returns every finding with its source, read-only next steps and what was not analysed and why. When the input is a QUESTION about something this product does, `answeredBy` names the command that answers it and why -- a question about exposure and node access is answered by `posture scan`, not by reading pods. It is empty whenever the input was recognised as something pasted, and empty for a sentence reporting a malfunction, because the diagnosis above it is the answer to those. Read-only, local.

post.summary: Audit manifests against the rules for a platform and version
post.description: Full deterministic audit: security, network exposure, storage access modes, reliability and red-team scenarios. Findings carry rule ids, line numbers, fixes, citations and matching RHACS policy names. Read what was NOT decided as part of the answer: `assumptions`, `declined` (per rule, the objects it could not read and why), controlSummary.notEvaluatedRules (rules that reached no verdict: neither clean nor findings) and controlSummary.partlyEvaluatedRules (rules that found something and declined on other objects). On a large manifest set pass compact=true: the same report, with each rule's constants hoisted once into ruleInfo instead of repeated on every finding, which is lossless and about a third smaller.

post.description: Match an error or symptom against the issues listed in the OpenShift release notes (known issues and issues fixed in each update) and, when this install keeps a local copy of Red Hat's public Jira, against those tickets too. Returns the issue id and link, what became of it (fixed and in which version, still open, closed as not a bug, won't fix or a duplicate), the workaround and Red Hat's remarks from the comments; with `version`, only issues that can affect that version.

post.summary: Risks Red Hat declares for an OpenShift update, offline
post.description: Before updating OpenShift from one x.y.z version to another: the risks Red Hat declares for that update in the public update graph (conditional updates, as an OpenShift Update Service serves them), from a bundled snapshot, offline. Each risk has its name, message, link, the version that fixes it and a verdict: applies (declared for every cluster), check (one fact decides it, with the read-only command or must-gather file that shows it) or cannot evaluate offline (its PromQL, as written). Whether the update is in your channel is not checked.

post.summary: Can pod A reach pod B under these NetworkPolicies?
post.description: Evaluate NetworkPolicies offline: can the source reach the destination on this port? Checks egress from the source and ingress to the destination, names the policy and rule that decide each, says why the other rules did not match, and proposes the smallest NetworkPolicy that would allow it.

post.summary: Lint legacy Kyverno policies for the CEL types: drafts and kyverno test skeletons, never applied
post.description: Kyverno 1.20 removes the kyverno.io ClusterPolicy, Policy, CleanupPolicy and legacy PolicyException. Lint them rule by rule against the policies.kyverno.io types: direct, inverted (a deny or a negated pattern: the CEL validation must state what is allowed), manual (JMESPath, API calls, anchors, strategic merge patches) or blocked (no documented CEL equivalent), each with the field path, the target kind, the reason and the Kyverno documentation section (pinned commit). Rules that map directly get a draft CEL policy and a kyverno test fixture skeleton to prove it. Nothing is applied or rewritten.

post.summary: What is wrong in a must-gather on the server's volume
post.description: Open an OpenShift must-gather (or oc adm inspect output) safely and say what is wrong, most severe first: the cluster version and update, cluster operators, nodes, machine config pools, OLM operators, pods, warning events and etcd log hints, and an installed-operator inventory. Each finding has its evidence file, its signals, read-only commands to confirm it, and the known OpenShift bugs and team memory entries that match it for the version the cluster runs. Nothing is extracted or run and Secrets are never read. Paths must be inside /srv/kube-noob/must-gather.

post.summary: Alertmanager webhook receiver: post the payload, get (and keep) an evidence report per alert
post.description: One report per alert in an Alertmanager payload: the signals it carries, the diagnosis kube-noob's playbooks give, the reported OpenShift issues that match for the version its labels name, approved team memory when configured, and read-only next steps. Every section says what it could not determine and why; an alert kube-noob recognises nothing in is reported as such, never as healthy, and a resolved alert is recorded, not diagnosed. Offline, from the payload alone: no cluster is read. This tool keeps no report (like diagnose it counts the playbook and issue ids it matched in the local learning file); the HTTP receiver POST /v1/alert-reports stores the same report.
